label: Rune
notes: A session builds the whole engine (nothing shared between sessions), applies its limits, registers the host call function, then evaluates 1 + 1 and reads 2 back in Rust. Limits: runtime::budget::with(1000000000 instructions) and alloc::limit::with(64MiB) around every Vm call; Context::with_default_modules (no fs/process/net modules).
Memory: resident growth across 1,000 live sessions (stopped by target), measured first in a fresh process.

Tool call: the guest calls a registered Rust function on its own stack. Median of per-batch means, 1,000,000 calls in batches of 1,000 after 100,000 warm-ups; mean 0.6649 µs, slowest batch 0.9534 µs per call; 0.6649 µs of CPU per call.

Session = Context::with_default_modules() + module with call + RuntimeContext + compiled Unit + Vm; nothing shared across sessions, so start includes building the default-module context and compiling `pub fn main() { 1 + 1 }`.

Host fn is Module::function("call", fn(&Object) -> VmResult<Object>); Rune objects key on heap-allocated rune::alloc::String, so each reply allocates three key strings (the guest's object literals do the same).
Tool-call guest is compiled into a second Unit in the same Context/RuntimeContext and run by its own Vm.
Compute: not measured in the Rust host.
